{{Short description|Theorem in functional analysis}}
In mathematics, and particularly in [[functional analysis]], '''Fichera's existence principle''' is an existence and uniqueness theorem for solution of [[functional (mathematics)|functional equations]], proved by [[Gaetano Fichera]] in 1954.<ref>{{harv|Faedo|1957|p=1}}, {{harv|Valent|1999|p=84}}, {{harv|Leonardi|Passarelli di Napoli|Sbordone|2000|p=221}}.</ref> More precisely, given a general [[vector space]] {{mvar|'''''V'''''}} and two [[linear map]]s from it [[Surjective function|onto]] two [[Banach space]]s, the principle states necessary and sufficient conditions for a [[linear transformation]] between the two [[Dual space#Continuous dual space|dual]] Banach spaces to be invertible for every vector in {{mvar|'''''V'''''}}.<ref>See {{harvs|last=Fichera|year=1955|year2=1958|loc=pp. 175–177|loc2=pp. 30–35}}, {{harv|Faedo|1957|pp=1–2}}, {{harv|Miranda|1970|pp=123–124}}, {{harv|Valent|1999|p=84}}.</ref>
